action: Check every NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus server that serves HTTP/2. Apply the fixed versions from F5 bulletins K000163926 and K000163928, or disable HTTP/2 until patched (this covers only the HTTP/2 flaws; the resolver, HTTP/3 and mail proxy flaws need the fixed versions, 1.30.7 or 1.31.9) (remove http2 from the listen line, or set http2 off on 1.25.0 and earlier). Review exposed servers for signs of compromise.
exec: NGINX is among the most widely used web servers and proxies; an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw with a public proof of concept makes exposed servers urgent to patch or mitigate.
plain: French cyber agency warns of two flaws in the NGINX web server that could let an attacker run code on a server over HTTP/2, with public attack code available for one of them.

key_findings: Two flaws, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2.
Affected: NGINX Open Source 1.31.x before 1.31.9 and versions before 1.30.7; NGINX Plus 3.1.x-3.2.x before 3.7.3.0.1 and 3.7.x before 37.0.8.1.
CERT-FR knows of a public proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007; in-the-wild exploitation is not stated.

KrCERT/CC lists five NGINX Plus and Open Source flaws fixed by F5: CVE-2026-123007 (integer underflow) and use-after-free CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810 and CVE-2026-113425; it urges updating to the fixed versions (Open Source 1.30.7 or 1.31.9). nginx.org titles them: CVE-2026-123007 memory corruption in HTTP/2 flow control (major); CVE-2026-123633 use-after-free in HTTP/2 (medium); CVE-2026-123634 use-after-free in the resolver (medium); CVE-2026-121810 use-after-free in HTTP/3 (medium); CVE-2026-113425 use-after-free in the mail proxy module (major).
recommendations: Disable HTTP/2 as an interim workaround for the HTTP/2 flaws only; it does not mitigate the resolver, HTTP/3 or mail proxy flaws.

summary: CERT-FR warns that two flaws in F5 NGINX, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; a public proof of concept exists for CVE-2026-123007. Fixed in Open Source 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Palo Alto Networks says PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled are affected and it is not aware of malicious exploitation. Disabling HTTP/2 is an interim workaround for those two flaws.
title: CERT-FR: NGINX flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution over HTTP/2; public PoC exists

validation.note: Compared CERT-FR (primary) with Rapid7 (PoC author): CVE-2026-123007 HTTP/2 flaw, fixes 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, public PoC, no in-the-wild exploitation stated. Rapid7 notes its PoC needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 data and a specific x86-64 glibc, and gives no HTTP/2-off workaround; that workaround is CERT-FR advice. Not compared: CVE-2026-123633 (only CERT-FR).

review.note: CERT-FR (date, CVEs, versions, PoC for 123007, HTTP/2 workaround, bulletins), Palo Alto, Rapid7 PoC, nginx.org, KrCERT, Wiz, GBHackers, SecurityWeek agree; no in-the-wild exploitation claimed
